atoms.text: Hindus around the world look forward to Diwali each year. Diwali is celebrated some time in October or November. The exact date changes from year to year and is based on the Hindu calendar. Diwali is known as “the festival of lights”, and Hindus decorate their homes and businesses with lamps and special lights. Celebrations also include the exchange of gifts, fireworks and dressing up in special clothes. Diwali celebrates the story of the great warrior prince Rama and his defeat of the evil king Ravana.

atoms.text: For Muslims, Eid-ul-Fitr celebrates the end of the holy month of Ramadan. During Ramadan, Muslims fast from sunrise to sunset every day throughout the month. Fasting means not eating or drinking. They also devote more time to prayer, helping the needy and spending time with family. On the day of Eid-ul-Fitr, Muslims attend a special service at their Mosque, give gifts to children and share a special meal. On Eid, Muslims wish each other “Eid Mubarak” which means “have a blessed holiday”.

atoms.text: Vesak is celebrated by Buddhists each May on the full moon. Vesak marks the birth of the Buddha. Buddhists celebrate Vesak with prayer, chanting and visiting the temple. Buddhists often mark the occasion with the “bathing of the Buddha” ceremony, during which they pour water over the statue of the Buddha.
